title: TORX® with Kailas 2026 – Regulations (English version)
claims: The regulations describe the races as taking place in a single stage, at free speed, within a limited time, under a semi-self-sufficiency regime.

TOR330 is described as a route of approximately 350 km with around 25,000 m of positive gain evaluated by ITRA, crossing 34 municipalities on official trails of Valle d'Aosta, with refreshment points every 7/10 km and six Life Bases in Valgrisenche, Cogne, Donnas, Gressoney SJ, Valtournenche and Ollomont.
The maximum time allowed for TOR330 is 150 hours.
The entry fee for TOR330 is 990 euros, the maximum number of bibs is 1,100, and entry is open from age 20.
ITRA rates TOR330 at 6 ITRA points and 12 mountain points.
All official refreshment points are also checkpoints, and failure to register leads to disqualification.
Official refreshment points supply drinks and food strictly for runners, to be consumed on site; plastic cups are not supplied and runners must carry a cup or container.
Some refreshment points allow a short rest of a maximum of two hours.
Life Bases provide a full hot meal and a hot shower and allow a longer rest within the time barriers; access is for runners only and all Life Bases require check-in and check-out.
It is forbidden to sleep in any structure, shelter or vehicle outside areas designated and controlled by the organisation.
TOR bags are transferred between Life Bases by the organisation and must be collected and returned in person.
A runner who withdraws must report the decision at the nearest checkpoint, and the organisation arranges transport back to the Life Base in Courmayeur.
Helicopter transfer is only for patients requiring urgent medical attention and cannot be used by runners who withdraw.
Any personal assistance along the route, and any pacing, leads to disqualification.
Each Life Base has an entry and an exit time barrier, and runners may not leave after the limit has expired.
The organisation may postpone or cancel the race in unfavourable or extreme weather conditions.

TOR330 mandatory equipment covers a cup, a mobile phone kept on, an identity document, two survival blankets, food and water supplies and two head torches with spare batteries; the handheld GPS navigator, route maps, altimeter and compass are listed only in the TOR450 column.
